title: Church-land rezoning hearing and committee overhaul
subtitle: Waterloo Park plan, 143 Columbia towers, heritage designations, stormwater rules, water-ownership resolution, William Street Pumping Station reuse.
overview: Council's long meeting centred on an informal public meeting about a city-initiated zoning change that would expand housing and community-use permissions on 14 places of worship. No decision was made; staff will report back after summer engagement. Many residents objected, citing notice problems, neighbourhood fit and green space, and several said owners had not asked to be included.

Council approved a review of its committees {{vote:m14}}. It will move the Sustainability Advisory Committee and the Waterloo Advisory Committee on Active Transportation to working-group models and set an automatic annual honorarium. A proposal to bar relatives of sitting councillors from advisory committees was defeated {{vote:m13}}. Council also approved rezoning for three towers at 143 Columbia Street West {{vote:m17}}, notices of intention to designate five heritage properties {{vote:m15}}, and new sanitary and stormwater by-laws {{vote:m8}}.

Council also released funding for the Waterloo Park plan {{vote:m3}}, moved the William Street Pumping Station reuse project forward {{vote:m12}}, and passed a resolution supporting public ownership of water and wastewater services {{vote:m18}}. A closed session on a staff matter and water legal advice was held, and the minutes report no public outcome.

decisions.detail: Council approved the zoning amendment for the three-tower development at 143 Columbia Street West {{vote:m17}}.
Council approved the committee policy changes, converted two advisory committees to working groups at the end of their terms, and set a $250 automatic annual honorarium {{vote:m14}}.
Council defeated an amendment that would have barred relatives of sitting council members from advisory committees {{vote:m13}}.
Council directed the Clerk to issue notices of intention to designate five King Street and John Street properties under the Ontario Heritage Act {{vote:m15}}.
Council approved the Sanitary and Stormwater Services By-law and the Stormwater Utility and Credit Program By-law {{vote:m8}}.
Council directed staff to proceed with a constraints assessment, community engagement and a request for expressions of interest for reuse, and released $50,000 in funding {{vote:m12}}.
Council released $567,000 in 2026 capital funding for Waterloo Park plan implementation {{vote:m3}}.
Council affirmed support for public ownership of water and wastewater services and asked the province to review Schedule 16 of Bill 60 {{vote:m18}}.

debate: Delegates and some councillors said blanket zoning of 14 church properties skips the usual site-specific studies, and questioned why these sites were chosen when owners had not asked for the change.

Residents raised notice concerns: many near one site said they received no mailed notice, signs were not up, and the comment deadline date was confusing. Staff said notices met Planning Act distances and committed to installing signs.

A child care operator asked for protection of an existing licensed centre at one church; staff said that would be a matter between the owner and tenant but hoped child care could be preserved or expanded. A supporter of the proposal pointed to homelessness and housing waitlists and urged affordability requirements.

On committees, staff said working groups would be more flexible and project-focused, while one councillor wanted a council liaison treated as close to mandatory. Opponents of the relatives restriction said no problem had been shown.

On 143 Columbia, councillors questioned the reduced tower separation, the pedestrian connection across private land, bike parking and affordable units. Staff and the applicant's planner said the layout separates pedestrian and vehicle traffic and that affordability and unit mix could be addressed at site plan.
